title: Bruhat factors with explicit inversion-root support
statement:
Let $A$ be a nonzero commutative ring, $P=(G,T=D_A(M),\Phi,\Phi^\vee,\Delta,(X_\alpha))$ a pinned split realization over $A$ [def-sfb-pinned-split-root-realization], and $A\to F$ a ring homomorphism to an algebraically closed field. Use the root subgroups $U_c$, closed-root-set subgroups $U_\Psi$, positive and negative systems $\pm\Phi^+$, and constant Weyl group $W=N_G(T)/T$ of [lem-sfb-split-root-subgroup-weyl-calculus], and write $G_F$, $T_F$, $(U_\Psi)_F$ for the base changes along $\operatorname{Spec}F\to\operatorname{Spec}A$. For each $w\in W$ choose any representative $n_w\in N_G(T)(F)$ of $w$. Put $I_w=\{c\in\Phi^+:w^{-1}c\in-\Phi^+\}$, a closed root set, and $U^+=U_{\Phi^+}$. Multiplication identifies
$$(U_{I_w})_F\times_F T_F\times_F U^+_F\longrightarrow G_F,\qquad (v,t,u)\longmapsto v n_w t u$$
with a locally closed subscheme $D_w$ of $G_F$, and the $D_w$ for $w\in W$ form a disjoint partition of the underlying space of $G_F$. In particular every $g\in G(F)$ has such a factorization for a unique $w$. The assertions hold for every such homomorphism $A\to F$, in particular after every algebraically closed extension of $F$, and for every choice of representatives; the case $A=F$ is included. There is an element $w_0\in W$ with $w_0\Phi^+=-\Phi^+$ and $w_0^{-1}=w_0$. Empty roots are permitted, giving $W=\{1\}$, $U^+=1$ and $G_F=T_F$.

source.place: Definition 21.76, Proposition 21.77 (136) and Lemma 21.78, pp.448--449; Theorem 21.80(a),(b) and Definition 21.81, p.450: $U^w=U\cap n_wU^-n_w^{-1}$ is the product of the $U_\alpha$ with $\alpha\in\Phi^+$ and $w^{-1}\alpha\in-\Phi^+$, multiplication $U^w\times B\to U^wn_wB$ is an isomorphism, and $G=\bigsqcup_wU^wn_wB$. Also Conrad, Reductive Group Schemes, Theorem 1.4.12, printed p.38 (read online by the worker; archival copy WANTED). No Stacks tag states Bruhat decomposition.

proof.text: Fix $A\to F$. By [lem-sfb-pinned-split-root-base-change] the pullback is a pinned split realization of the same based datum, even when $A\to F$ is not flat. In the rest of the proof write $G,T,U_\Psi$ for their pullbacks to $F$. The root maps and closed-root-set product charts are the pulled-back ones by [lem-sfb-split-root-subgroup-weyl-calculus]. Choose a rational linear functional on $M\otimes\mathbf Q$ taking value $1$ on each simple root: extend the linearly independent set $\Delta$ to a rational basis, assign zero to the other basis vectors, and clear denominators on a lattice basis of $M$. This gives $\lambda\in M^\vee$ with $\langle\alpha,\lambda\rangle>0$ for every positive root. The same-sign simple-root expansions show that it is nonzero on every root. By [def-sfb-pinned-split-root-realization] this integer functional is a cocharacter of $T$.

source.place: 21.17, p.431 (base-change root datum); 21.29--21.32, pp.433--435 (choice of regular cocharacter).

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-regular-cocharacter-borel-description], $B=P(\lambda)$ is a Borel containing $T$ with positive roots exactly $\Phi^+$. By [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure], its radical $V$ gives $B=V\rtimes T$ and the right torsor $\pi:G\to Q=G/B$. The root subgroups in the field-theoretic nodes coincide with our pulled-back root groups: both are smooth connected $T$-stable subgroups with tangent line $\mathfrak g_\alpha$, so the uniqueness statement of [lem-sfb-reductive-root-subgroup-parametrizations] applies. By [lem-sfb-borel-root-product-coordinates] and the product charts in [lem-sfb-split-root-subgroup-weyl-calculus], both $V$ and $U^+$ are the image of the same ordered product of positive root groups. Hence $V=U^+$ as subgroup schemes. Multiplication $T\times U^+\to B$ is an isomorphism: if the usual coordinates are $b=ut$, its inverse is $b\mapsto(t,t^{-1}ut)$, using that $T$ normalizes $U^+$.

source.place: Theorem 21.68(a), pp.445--446; Summary 21.86, p.451; 21.19, p.431, for uniqueness of the root groups.

proof.text: Identify the constant $W$ with $N_G(T)(F)/T(F)$. Indeed [lem-sfb-split-root-subgroup-weyl-calculus] says that the quotient sheaf is constant and is generated by the simple reflections, each lifted by its displayed $n_\alpha\in N_G(T)(F)$. Products lift every $w$, and the kernel on $F$-points is $T(F)$. Any representative differs from such a product by a torus point. The same node says that conjugation by each $n_\alpha$ sends $U_c$ onto $U_{s_\alpha c}$; its torus-equivariance formula says torus points preserve every root group. Thus every chosen $n_w$ conjugates $U_c$ onto $U_{wc}$. Put $B'_w=n_wBn_w^{-1}$. This is a Borel containing $T$ with positive roots $w\Phi^+$: conjugation is a group-scheme isomorphism and its full character action, not a differentiated character, sends $c$ to $wc$.

source.place: 21.1 and 21.17--21.19, pp.426,431; paragraph preceding Proposition 21.70, p.446 (normalizer representatives and action).

proof.text: Put $J_w=\Phi^+\cap w\Phi^+$, so $\Phi^+=I_w\sqcup J_w$. The set $I_w$ is closed in the required sense: a root which is a nonempty sum of its elements is positive, while its inverse image under $w$ is a nonempty sum of negative roots and hence negative, by the same-sign coordinates in the simple-root basis. In particular it contains no opposite pair. By [lem-sfb-unipotent-root-intersection-products], the subgroup scheme $H_w=U^+\cap B'_w$ is the ordered product of the $U_c$ for $c\in J_w$, in any order. By [lem-sfb-split-root-subgroup-weyl-calculus], the corresponding product for $I_w$ is $U_{I_w}$. Order all positive roots with $I_w$ first and $J_w$ second. The all-orders product isomorphism of [lem-sfb-borel-root-product-coordinates] then gives an isomorphism of schemes $U_{I_w}\times H_w\xrightarrow{\sim}U^+$, $(v,h)\mapsto vh$. Right multiplication by $H_w$ changes only the second coordinate, so the first-coordinate projection is its quotient map.

source.place: Definition 21.76, Proposition 21.77 (136), Lemma 21.78 and Definition 21.81, pp.448--450. Use ordered root coordinates rather than treating multiplication of these two subgroups as a homomorphism.

proof.text: Let $e_w=n_wB\in Q(F)$. The torsor identity in [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure] gives, on every test algebra, $\operatorname{Stab}_{U^+}(e_w)=U^+\cap n_wBn_w^{-1}=H_w$. The orbit $O_w=U^+e_w$ with its reduced structure is a smooth locally closed subscheme of $Q$, by [lem-sfb-smooth-group-orbit-geometry]. Its hypotheses hold: $U^+$ is smooth connected affine of finite type by its root coordinates, and $Q$ is separated of finite type since it is proper over $F$. By [lem-sfb-homogeneous-orbit-quotient-geometry], $O_w=U^+/H_w$ as the fppf quotient. The preceding product chart identifies this quotient with $U_{I_w}$: a coset represented by the unique product $vh$ is sent to $v$. This is independent of $h$, and the projection is invariant on every test algebra, so descends to the quotient sheaf. Its inverse sends $v$ to the coset of $v$. Consequently $v\mapsto vn_wB$ is an isomorphism $U_{I_w}\xrightarrow{\sim}O_w$.

source.place: Proposition 21.79(a),(b), p.449; quotient and stabilizer argument made scheme-theoretic using the existing orbit and torsor nodes.

proof.text: Define $D_w=G\times_Q O_w$. It is a locally closed subscheme of $G$ by [lem-weil-pbc-immersion-base-change-lft](1). The isomorphism $U_{I_w}\to O_w$ has the lift $v\mapsto vn_w$ into $G$. The right torsor identity in [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure] now gives an isomorphism $U_{I_w}\times B\to D_w$, $(v,b)\mapsto vn_wb$. Explicitly, for a point $g$ over any test scheme, recover $v$ from $\pi(g)\in O_w$, then recover the unique $b\in B$ by $b=(vn_w)^{-1}g$. These are morphisms by the inverse orbit chart and the torsor isomorphism, and their two composites are identities. Substitute the isomorphism $T\times U^+\to B$ of step 2. The resulting isomorphism is exactly $(v,t,u)\mapsto vn_wtu$, including the order of its three variable factors.

source.place: Theorem 21.80(b), p.450; its inverse is written on all test schemes. Immersion base change: Stacks tag 01JY, schemes.tex, lemma-base-change-immersion.

proof.text: The orbits $O_w$ are pairwise disjoint. To see that their labels are distinct, use the cocharacter $\mu$ from [lem-sfb-flag-torus-fixed-geometry], positive on $\Phi^+$, whose fixed points $e_w$ are indexed without repetition by $W$. In the equivariant product coordinates of [lem-sfb-borel-root-product-coordinates], conjugation by $\mu(t)$ multiplies the coordinate of $U_c$ by $t^{\langle c,\mu\rangle}$. All exponents are positive. Thus for any algebraically closed extension $K/F$ and $v\in U^+(K)$ the orbit of $ve_w$ has limit $e_w$ at $0$. A point in both $O_w(K)$ and $O_z(K)$ would therefore give $e_w=e_z$: two extensions of the same orbit map to $\mathbf A^1_K$ agree because $Q_K$ is separated. Thus $w=z$. For exhaustion use only the stated stratification in [lem-sfb-bruhat-longest-cell-charts]. Each of its strata has coordinates $(a,b)\mapsto an_zb$ with $a$ in a subscheme of $U^+$; therefore every geometric point of $G$ maps under $\pi$ into some $O_z$. This proves that the locally closed $D_w=\pi^{-1}(O_w)$ cover the entire underlying space and are disjoint. In particular each $g\in G(F)$ has the asserted factorization, with unique $w$ (and unique coordinates for that $w$).

source.place: Propositions 21.70--21.71 and Theorem 21.73(a), pp.446--447; Theorem 21.80(a), p.450. Reuse the existing exhaustion theorem, without assuming its unspecified subschemes $V^w$ identify the inversion-root factors.

proof.text: The same Bruhat-chart node [lem-sfb-bruhat-longest-cell-charts] supplies $w_0\Phi^+=-\Phi^+$ and $w_0^2=1$, which is $w_0^{-1}=w_0$. All the preceding steps apply to every map $A\to F$; their fibrewise hypotheses are supplied by the base-change statement in step 1. For an algebraically closed extension $K/F$, the displayed coordinate isomorphisms pull back to the same multiplication maps. The intersection node [lem-sfb-unipotent-root-intersection-products] preserves $H_w$ and its root description, and the Bruhat-chart node preserves exhaustion. The distinct-limit argument of step 7 works over $K$ verbatim, giving the asserted partition after extension. Finally if $n'_w=n_wa$ with $a\in T(F)$, the substitution $(v,t,u)\mapsto(v,a^{-1}t,u)$ gives the identical element using $n'_w$; this is an invertible scheme coordinate change. Empty roots cause no exception: [lem-sfb-regular-cocharacter-borel-description] gives $G=T$, the root products are trivial, and $W=\{1\}$ by the root-calculus node. The sole map is translation on $T$.
